strengths: Well-motivated problem with compelling empirical evidence of overthinking in LRLMs (~75% of samples have early-exit solutions)
Practical training-free approach that seamlessly integrates with existing reasoning models without fine-tuning
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across 6 benchmarks, 4 model sizes, with consistent 1.7-5.7% accuracy improvements and 31-43% token reduction
Thorough empirical analysis including fine-grained sample categorization, threshold robustness, and ablation studies on transition signals
Strong end-to-end latency improvements (43.4-47.3% reduction) with practical applicability
Clear presentation with effective visualizations and algorithm pseudocode
weaknesses: Limited novelty: straightforward application of confidence-based early stopping with simple mean-of-max-token-probabilities metric; concurrent work with similar motivation suggests incremental contribution
Requires manual per-model/domain threshold tuning with no principled method for selection on new domains without validation data
Model-specific limitations: method fails on QwQ-32B where ⟨/think⟩ delimiters don't reliably control exit, raising generalization concerns
Incomplete submission: references missing 'Table X' for prompt design combinations and notes 'More discussion about end-to-end latency will be added in forthcoming version'
Confidence metric (mean of max token probabilities) fails for programming tasks due to fixed-pattern tokens approaching probability 1, explaining poor BigCodeBench results (0.2-point improvement)
Circular motivation analysis: 'pearl reasoning' evaluation uses oracle ground-truth information; doesn't address inference-time identification without labels
Limited baseline comparisons: primarily compares vanilla CoT without quantitative comparison to other efficient reasoning methods (Budget Forcing, prompt-based approaches)
No statistical rigor: single-run results without error bars, confidence intervals, or multiple-run variance analysis
Computational overhead of trial answer generation not thoroughly analyzed; branch-parallel decoding solution left vague and incomplete
Insufficient error analysis: limited discussion of failure modes and characteristics of samples amenable to early exit

strengths: Clear and well-motivated problem identification with the 'pearl reasoning' concept effectively demonstrated through exploratory experiments
Practical and training-free approach that is easy to implement and integrate into existing reasoning models
Comprehensive evaluation across multiple model sizes (1.5B-32B) and diverse benchmarks (math, science, programming tasks)

Consistent improvements on DeepSeek-R1 distilled models with detailed ablations and analysis (threshold sensitivity, transition token variants, fine-grained categorization of correct/incorrect transitions)
End-to-end latency measurements showing 43-47% reduction when measured without acceleration frameworks
weaknesses: Limited novelty: the core contribution (confidence-based early stopping at transition tokens) is a straightforward extension of budget forcing with insufficient differentiation from concurrent work (Zhang et al., 2025; Ma et al., 2025a)
Missing critical baselines: no comparison with budget forcing (most directly related method), other efficient reasoning approaches, or simple alternatives like fixed-percentage exits

Crude and unreliable confidence metric: mean of max token probabilities is known to have calibration issues; paper acknowledges that programming tasks exhibit artificial high confidence due to fixed patterns, yet this is not addressed

Ad-hoc threshold selection with no principled methodology: different λ values needed for different tasks, substantial accuracy variance (5-10 points) across reasonable thresholds, and no protocol for selecting λ for new models without labeled validation data
Poor generalization to QwQ-32B: achieves only 24% length reduction with 3 additional errors, suggesting the method is fragile across model variants; limited to DeepSeek-R1 distilled models

Incomplete efficiency analysis: branch-parallel decoding claims are unvalidated empirically; latency measurements lack integration with modern frameworks (vLLM); overhead from confidence computation not accounted for

Unclear mechanism: no evidence that 'Wait' tokens are optimal transition points (Table 2 shows 'Alternatively' outperforms by 3.7 points but exits less frequently); why early exit improves accuracy is not rigorously established
Statistical rigor lacking: no error bars, confidence intervals, or significance testing; some improvements are marginal (1.0-1.4 points) and potentially noise; only greedy decoding evaluated
Missing ablation studies: no comparison of exit with/without confidence checking, different answer inducer prompts, or simpler baselines
Incomplete content: branch-parallel acceleration details promised for 'forthcoming version'; missing Table X on prompt combination; no code availability mentioned for reproducibility

strengths: Well-motivated problem with empirical validation: motivational analysis convincingly demonstrates 75% of samples contain sufficient reasoning before completion, providing strong foundation
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple benchmarks (MATH-500, AMC 2023, GPQA Diamond, AIME 2024, HumanEval, BigCodeBench) and model sizes (1.5B-32B) with consistent improvements
Strong empirical results: 31-43% average token reduction with 1.7-5.7% accuracy improvements, including substantial gains (e.g., 10.6 points on GPQA Diamond)
Practical training-free method that seamlessly integrates into existing reasoning models, enabling real-world deployment
Fine-grained analysis and ablation studies: provides useful insights into failure modes, hyperparameter sensitivity, and impact of design choices
Actual latency measurements (43-47% reduction) demonstrating real-world efficiency gains beyond token count
Clear presentation with effective visualizations and case studies illustrating the method's behavior
weaknesses: Limited novelty: core contribution is straightforward application of confidence thresholding at transition points, an incremental extension of budget forcing; authors acknowledge concurrent similar work

Incomplete efficiency analysis: branch-parallel decoding acceleration (Section 4.2) explicitly noted as unfinished ('More discussion will be added in forthcoming version'), undermining efficiency claims

Poor generalization to diverse architectures: QwQ-32B results (24% token reduction, 3 additional errors) concerning; QwQ-32B's non-compliance with </think> delimiter suggests architecture-dependent fragility

Oversimplified confidence metric: mean token probability is crude, especially for variable-length answers; paper acknowledges failure for programming but offers no solution; no exploration of alternatives
Threshold λ lacks principled selection: requires per-benchmark tuning, varies across datasets, no guidance for threshold selection without validation data
Circular validation of 'pearl reasoning': motivational analysis forces early exits to validate concept, but doesn't prove confidence-based early exit is the correct mechanism

Insufficient failure analysis: limited discussion of when/why early exit produces errors (red bars in Figure 5); high sensitivity to transition point choice (Table 2: Wait vs Alternatively differ 3.7 points in accuracy, 12% in length)
Shallow theoretical justification: paper provides intuition but lacks formal analysis of why answer confidence at transition points indicates reasoning sufficiency
Reproducibility concerns: missing implementation details (e.g., exact 'Wait' token detection), no code release mentioned, sparse hyperparameter documentation
Limited statistical rigor: no confidence intervals or significance tests; small benchmark sizes (AIME 30, AMC 40 samples) with unclear statistical robustness

strengths: Well-motivated empirical analysis with compelling evidence for pearl reasoning (Figures 1-2)
Comprehensive evaluation across 11 diverse reasoning models and 10 benchmarks spanning mathematics, science, and programming domains
Training-free approach that is practical and immediately deployable to existing models
Consistent improvements: 19.1%-80.1% sequence length reduction while maintaining/improving accuracy
Thorough ablation studies examining transition monitors, threshold robustness, and confidence averaging methods
Solid technical contributions including DEER-Pro robustness analysis via signal-to-noise ratio theory
Multiple implementation variants and acceleration strategies (branch-parallel decoding)
weaknesses: Limited conceptual novelty: straightforward application of standard confidence-based early stopping to reasoning token generation
Weak causal justification: pilot experiments show forced early exit can work, but don't establish that model confidence reliably predicts correctness; connection is mostly correlational
Answer inducing prompts fundamentally alter the decoding path mid-generation; DEER-Pro requires 4 inference passes, eliminating efficiency gains for many scenarios

Hyperparameter threshold λ appears fixed at 0.95 across all experiments despite very different confidence distributions across models (Table 12); method fails on Llama-3.1-Nemotron with only 55% early exit rate
Weak baseline comparisons: TCC uses fixed prompts, NoThinking skips reasoning entirely, CoD severely limits steps; missing comparisons to other confidence-based methods or learned policies
Limited analysis of when/why method fails: programming tasks show minimal accuracy gains (0.1-0.3%), unclear false early exit rates
Generalization concerns: method relies on explicit <think> delimiters and linguistic markers; applicability to other reasoning architectures unclear
Incomplete efficiency analysis: latency improvements depend on implementation details; modest gains for code generation (19.9% vs 61.5% for math)
Code repository URL incomplete; some hyperparameter selection rationale unclear (e.g., entropy threshold 0.672, α=1 parameter)
Circular reasoning in robustness argument: method works because confidence separates well, so threshold robustness follows; doesn't guarantee generalization to new domains

strengths: Comprehensive experimental evaluation across 11 models and 10 benchmarks with consistent positive results across diverse reasoning tasks
Thorough ablation studies and sensitivity analyses with error bars and statistical rigor
Training-free plug-and-play method requiring no model modification or retraining
Well-articulated motivation addressing genuine redundancy in long CoT sequences
Detailed implementation details and reproducibility information provided
weaknesses: Limited novelty: core method (detect transitions → induce answers → check confidence → exit) straightforwardly combines existing techniques without fundamental innovation
Circular definition of 'pearl reasoning'—defined essentially as 'positions where early exit works' rather than formally characterized
Methodological gaps: geometric mean confidence metric lacks principled justification; threshold λ=0.95 appears ad-hoc; entropy threshold (0.672) relies on external heuristic without validation
Missing wall-clock time measurements in main results (reported only in Figure 7)—only token counts shown despite being critical for practical deployment
Poor generalization: Llama-3.1-Nemotron exhibits 55% exit rate vs 80-85% for others, suggesting method may not work broadly across architectures
Limited baseline comparisons: no simple baselines (fixed exit positions, length heuristics); chosen baselines appear to highlight DEER's advantages
Small-scale benchmarks: AMC (40 samples) and AIME (30 samples) despite multiple runs; marginal improvements (0.3-1%) may be within noise given multiple comparisons
Greedy decoding only in main experiments—practical sampling results relegated to appendix despite being more realistic
DEER-Pro requires 4× parallel forward passes, partially offsetting CoT reduction benefits; trade-off not clearly quantified
Critical insights (confidence polarization phenomenon, robustness explanation) hidden in 40+ page appendix; main paper reads as extended abstract
Insufficient analysis of why confidence scores correlate with correctness; limited failure case discussion; poor investigation of interaction with model size/architecture
Case studies (Figures 13-16) appear cherry-picked; no examples showing DEER's mistakes or limitations

strengths: Addresses important and timely problem of overthinking in reasoning models with strong empirical motivation
Comprehensive evaluation across 11 diverse reasoning models and 10 benchmarks with consistent improvements (0.3-5.0% accuracy, 19.1-80.1% compression)
Training-free, immediately applicable to existing models without fine-tuning
Well-executed technical approach with dual monitoring strategies and DEER-Pro variant backed by theoretical analysis
Robust methodology with multiple sampling rounds, confidence intervals, and extensive ablations
Significant practical impact: 27.9%-58.6% latency speedup, ready for deployment
Thorough analysis of design choices and failure modes with compelling case studies demonstrating mechanism effectiveness
weaknesses: Limited conceptual novelty - core idea of confidence-based early exit is relatively straightforward
Confidence metric (geometric mean of token probabilities) lacks deep theoretical justification for why token-level probabilities predict answer correctness
Generalization concerns: significant performance variance across models (Llama shows 55% exit rate vs 80-85% for others); evaluation limited to math/science/code domains
Incomplete failure mode analysis - limited systematic investigation of when early exits are incorrect and what problem characteristics lead to failures
Threshold selection still requires manual tuning (λ=0.95); no principled adaptive method despite claimed robustness in 0.9-0.97 range
Trial answer inducing introduces computational overhead; method's behavior under very long reasoning chains (>16k tokens) unclear
Limited comparison with concurrent work (Zhang et al. 2025a) on trained probe approaches that achieve different accuracy-efficiency tradeoffs
